A M P This policy is a legal contract between you and us. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. If more than one auto is insured, premiums will be shown for each auto. If you pay the premiums when due and comply with the policy terms, Allstate , relying on the information you have given us, makes the following agreements with you.

L E Your policy applies only during the policy period. During this time, it applies to losses to the auto , accidents and occurrences within the United States of America, its territories or possessions or Canada, or between their ports. The policy period is shown on the Policy Declarations.

## When And Where The Policy Applies

## Changes

## Premium Changes

The premium for each auto is based on information Allstate has received from you or other sources. You agree to cooperate with us in determining if this information is correct, if it is complete, and if it changes during the policy period. You agree that if this information changes or is incorrect or incomplete, we may adjust your premium accordingly during the policy period.

Changes which result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rules. These include, but are not limited to:

1. autos insured by the policy, including changes in use.
2. drivers residing in your household, their ages or marital status.
3. coverages or coverage limits.
4. rating territory.
5. discount eligibility.

Any calculation or adjustment of your premium will be made using the rules, rates and forms in effect, and on file if required, for our use in your state.

## Coverage Changes

When Allstate broadens a coverage during the policy period without additional charge, you have the new feature if you have the coverage to which it applies. The new feature applies on the date the coverage change is effective in your state. Otherwise, the policy can be changed only by endorsement. Any change in your coverage will be made using the rules, rates and forms in effect, and on file if required, for our use in your state.

## Duty To Report Autos

You must tell us within 60 days when you acquire an additional or replacement auto. If you don't, certain coverages of this policy may not apply.

## COMBININGLIMITS OF TWO OR MORE AUTOS PROHIBITED

IF YOU HAVE TWO OR MORE AUTOS INSURED IN YOUR NAME AND ONE OF THESE AUTOS IS INVOLVED IN AN ACCIDENT, ONLY THE COVERAGE LIMITS SHOWN ON THE POLICY DECLARATIONS FOR THAT AUTO WILL APPLY. WHEN YOU HAVE TWO OR MORE AUTOS INSURED IN YOUR NAME AND NONE OF THEM IS INVOLVED IN THE ACCIDENT, YOU MAY CHOOSE ANY SINGLE AUTO SHOWNONTHE POLICY DECL

ITY. THE LIMIT FOR LOSS TO ANY COVERED TRAILER NOT DESCRIBED ON THE POLICY DECLARATIONS IS $500.

P L AN AUTO AND ATTACHED TRAILER ARE CONSIDERED SEPARATE AUTOS, AND YOU MUST PAY THE DEDUCTIBLE, IF ANY, ON EACH. ONLY ONE DEDUCTIBLE WILL APPLY TO AN AUTO WITH A MOUNTED CAMPER UNIT. IF UNMOUNTED, A SEPARATE DEDUCTIBLE WILL APPLY TO THE AUTO AND CAMPER UNIT.

E IF THERE IS OTHER INSURANCE IF THERE IS OTHER INSURANCE COVERING THE LOSS AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT, WE WILL PAY ONLY OUR SHARE OF ANY DAMAGES. OUR SHARE IS DETERMINED BY ADDING THE LIMITS OF THIS INSURANCE TO THE LIMITS OF ALL OTHER INSURANCE THAT APPLIES ON THE SAME BASIS AND FINDING THE PERCENTAGE OF THE TOTAL THAT OUR LIMITS REPRESENT.

WHEN THIS INSURANCE COVERS A SUBSTITUTE AUTO OR NON-OWNED AUTO, WE WILL PAY ONLY AFTER ALL OTHER COLLECTIBLE INSURANCE HAS BEEN EXHAUSTED.

WHEN THIS INSURANCE COVERS A REPLACEMENT AUTO OR ADDITIONAL AUTO, THIS POLICY WON'T APPLY IF YOU HAVE OTHER COLLECTIBLE INSURANCE.

WHENMORETHANONECOVERAGE IS APPLICABLE TO THE LOSS, YOU MAY RECOVER UNDER THE BROADEST COVERAGE BUT NOT BOTH. HOWEVER, ANY COVERAGE ZA DEDUCTIBLE WILL ALWAYS APPLY.

## Action Against Allstate

No one may sue us under this coverage unless there is full compliance with all the policy terms.

## Subrogation Rights

When we pay, your rights of recovery from anyone else become ours up to the amount we have paid. You must protect these rights and help us enforce them.

## What You Must Do If There Is A Loss

1. As soon as possible, any person making claim must give us written proof of loss. It must include all details reasonably required by us. We have the right to inspect the damaged property. We may require any person making claim to file with us a sworn proof of loss. We may also require that person to submit to examinations under oath.
2. Protect the auto from further loss. We will pay reasonable expenses to guard against further loss. If you don't protect the auto, further loss is not covered.
3. Report all theft losses promptly to the police.

D IN WITNESS WHEREOF , Allstate has caused this policy to be signed by its Secretary and its President at Northbrook, Illinois, and if required by state law, this policy shall not be binding unless countersigned on the Policy Declarations by an authorized agent of Allstate.

Thought: The context states that a hit-and-run motor vehicle is an uninsured auto if it causes bodily injury to an insured person by physical contact with that person or with a vehicle occupied by that person. It also requires that the identity of the operator and owner be unknown or cannot be found, that the accident be reported as soon as possible to the proper authorities, and that the insurer be notified within 30 days. Additionally, the insured person must have the right to inspect the vehicle if they were occupying it at the time of the accident.

Answer: A hit-and-run vehicle is an uninsured auto if it causes bodily injury by physical contact with the insured person or a vehicle they occupy, and the identity of the operator and owner is unknown or cannot be found, the accident is reported as soon as possible to the proper authorities, and the insurer is notified within 30 days.
per_question.answer: A hit-and-run vehicle is an uninsured auto if it causes bodily injury by physical contact with the insured person or a vehicle they occupy, and the identity of the operator and owner is unknown or cannot be found, the accident is reported as soon as possible to the proper authorities, and the insurer is notified within 30 days.
per_question.judge_response:
The correct answer requires two things: physical contact with the insured person or their vehicle, and that the identity of the owner/operator is unknown. The LLM answer includes both of these core facts, essentially matching the correct answer’s meaning. It also adds extra conditions (reporting to authorities, notifying the insurer within 30 days), but these do not contradict the correct answer and are consistent with typical policy language. Since the core required elements are captured accurately, the answer should be scored as fully correct.

Thought: The context states that an insured person includes "You and any resident relative who sustains bodily injury while in, on, getting into or out of, or when struck by, an auto or trailer." It also defines "trailer" for certain coverage purposes as one attached to an insured auto and designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto. However, the medical payments insuring clause says "struck by, an auto or trailer" without requiring the trailer to be attached or designed for use with a private passenger auto in that specific phrase. The exclusions do not exclude being struck as a pedestrian by such a trailer. Therefore, the context supports coverage for an insured person struck as a pedestrian by a trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto.

Answer: Yes, an insured person is covered for medical payments if struck as a pedestrian by a trailer, as the policy covers bodily injury sustained when struck by an auto or trailer.

per_question.raw_response:
Thought: The context states in F3 that "bodily injury or property damage arising out of the use of a non-owned auto in any business or occupation of an insured person" is excluded "to the extent that the limits of liability for this coverage exceed the limits of liability required by the Nevada financial responsibility law." This means coverage is not eliminated entirely but is limited to the Nevada financial responsibility minimums. F14 further notes the exclusion does not apply while you, your chauffeur, or domestic servant are using a private passenger auto or trailer. So liability coverage may still apply up to the required minimum limits, and under certain private passenger auto/trailer exceptions the exclusion may not apply at all.

Answer: Yes, but only to the extent of the limits required by the Nevada financial responsibility law; coverage above those limits is excluded for business use of a non-owned auto, unless the exception for you, your chauffeur, or domestic servant using a private passenger auto or trailer applies.

per_question.judge_response:
The correct answer states that coverage generally does not apply for business use of a non-owned auto, except for a private passenger auto or trailer, and only up to Nevada state law limits if policy limits are higher.  
The LLM answer correctly notes the Nevada state law limit cap and the private passenger auto or trailer exception. However, it begins by saying “Yes,” which somewhat contradicts the general “no” in the correct answer, though it then qualifies it correctly. The core facts—limited to Nevada financial responsibility limits and the private passenger/trailer exception—are present. The main issue is framing, but the substantive coverage details match the correct answer. Given the rubric’s emphasis on meaning rather than wording, this is essentially correct.

per_question.gold: Nothing, as medical payments coverage does not apply to the extent treatment is covered by Workers Compensation.
